cur:objects-kells-market-cross.summary: The centre of the cross-head on the west face shows the Crucifixion, flanked on the arms by scenes from the lives of St Peter and of the desert fathers Paul and Anthony, including the Denial of Peter. Christ is set at the meeting point of the arms, the axis on which all the other stories turn. The cross once stood at the abbey's eastern gate, marking the threshold of the monastic town.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the 9th-century Market Cross originally stood at the abbey's eastern gate; legend says it was damaged by Cromwellian soldiers and used for hangings after the 1798 rebellion.
An inscription on its west face records its re-erection in 1688 (photographer's documentation).
